name: Bonapartism

authors.quote: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte ( Napoleon III , 1808–1873) used to construct and destroy a Second Empire

summary: Bonapartism is rule by a charismatic leader who claims to embody the people's will, combining a strong centralised state, army and bureaucracy with plebiscitary legitimacy. It promises to end revolutionary disorder and class conflict, reconcile authority with popular rights and 1789 equality, and deliver national glory and material progress through state-led growth, while suppressing organised opposition.
scope: The Napoleonic idea as set out by Louis-Napoléon in Des idées napoléoniennes (1839) and the 1852 constitution, and as practised in the Second Empire (1852-1870), with Napoleon I's tradition behind it. Excludes Marx's critical use of the word, the broad modern sense for any military strongman, and later neo-Bonapartist strands.
